sources.title: DGA 2025–2030: Daily Servings by Calorie Level
sources.attribution: Source: U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025–2030.

rights.scope: Attributed factual extraction and original educational paraphrases; no agency endorsement; no image or logo reuse in app. Original snapshots retained as research evidence.

entries.summary: DASH organizes food groups into an eating pattern whose portions depend on energy needs.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.summary: The source presents two daily sodium limits; neither is automatically assigned to a user.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Kidney disease or other medical requirements may change the target.

entries.summary: Favor whole grains for most grain servings.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.summary: The DASH pattern specifies low-fat or fat-free dairy.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Keep separate from DGA full-fat dairy guidance; do not merge by averaging.

entries.summary: DASH food-group servings and package-label servings are different measures.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.sourceLocator: Plan how much to eat or drink > Plate method
entries.summary: A plate-based meal pattern allocates half to nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter to carbohydrate foods and one quarter to protein.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: This is a meal-planning illustration, not a product score or carbohydrate prescription.

entries.summary: Carbohydrate counting considers amounts across meals and snacks. Not everyone with diabetes needs it.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Do not replace total carbohydrate with total sugars.
No insulin-dose calculation.

entries.summary: Discuss fiber-rich foods, unsweetened drinks and reducing sodium and saturated fat within a meal plan.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.sourceLocator: Find the best times to eat or drink
entries.summary: Meal timing depends on medicines, activity and other conditions.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Skipping or delaying meals may cause low glucose with some medicines; do not generate fasting schedules.

entries.sourceLocator: Plan how much to eat or drink
entries.summary: A care team can tailor the meal-planning method and portions.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Source does not provide one universal daily carbohydrate target.

entries.sourceLocator: How can I eat healthy with CKD?
entries.summary: CKD has no single diet; requirements change with kidney function and treatment.
entries.population: Adults with CKD; pediatric guidance is separate

entries.sourceLocator: Sodium; Choose and prepare foods with less salt and sodium
entries.summary: Compare sodium amounts, but obtain the individual limit from the care team.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: The page cites the older 2020–2025 DGA; retain that citation context rather than relabel it as 2025–2030.

entries.sourceLocator: Potassium; Choose foods that help keep your potassium level in the goal range
entries.summary: Potassium needs depend on blood levels; low-sodium substitutes may contain potassium chloride.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Do not automatically restrict potassium in every person with CKD.
Unknown potassium is not zero.

entries.sourceLocator: Choose foods and drinks with less phosphorus
entries.summary: Phosphate ingredients can flag added phosphorus, but do not quantify its amount.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Ingredient screening cannot establish total phosphorus or renal suitability.

entries.sourceLocator: Protein; Choose the amount and types of protein your body needs
entries.summary: Protein requirements vary; dialysis can increase needs.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Do not apply general-population protein targets automatically.

entries.summary: Fluid limits, when needed, depend on kidney function and clinical guidance.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Do not prescribe fluid restriction from a CKD checkbox.

entries.summary: The edition emphasizes nutrient-dense foods, varied produce, whole grains, water and unsweetened drinks.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.summary: The publication gives a body-weight-based protein range.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Not automatically applicable to CKD, dialysis, pregnancy or children.

entries.summary: The main publication favors full-fat dairy without added sugars.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: DASH differs; the supplementary servings guide also lists lower-fat dairy options. Preserve this distinction.

entries.summary: The general saturated-fat ceiling is expressed as a share of daily energy.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: A percentage of daily energy is not a per-product percentage-by-weight limit.

entries.sourceLocator: Printed p. 4: Limit Highly Processed Foods, Added Sugars, & Refined Carbohydrates
entries.summary: The edition discourages added sugars and states a per-meal ceiling.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: Total sugars cannot substitute for added sugars.
A ceiling is not a recommended intake.

entries.summary: Sodium guidance varies with age and notes high-activity exceptions.
entries.population: General population age 1+ as stated in source; automatic pediatric use excluded
exceptions: High sweat losses and clinical conditions require individual assessment.

entries.summary: Separate sections cover children, adolescents, pregnancy, lactation, older adults and chronic disease.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: No infant feeding, supplement dosing or pregnancy targets activated.

entries.sourceLocator: Printed p. 9: Individuals with Chronic Disease
entries.summary: The source directs people with chronic disease to discuss adaptations with their health professional.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.sourceLocator: Printed p. 1: Daily Servings by Calorie Level
entries.summary: Serving examples and energy-pattern tables use their own definitions; retain those definitions when comparing patterns.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription

entries.sourceLocator: Printed p. 2: FDA Healthy Claim: Added Sugar Limits
entries.summary: The supplement lists food-group-equivalent sugar limits; these alone do not establish eligibility for the full FDA claim.
entries.population: Adults; educational context, not a personal prescription
exceptions: No automatic Healthy label; additional criteria and primary FDA rules would need verification.

coverage: Nutrition guidance and structured reference tables from all four requested source families. Not an exhaustive executable transcription of every recommendation. Full source snapshots preserved.

conflicts.resolution: Unresolved for personalization. Keep plan-specific guidance; daily-serving appendix includes broader dairy options than the DGA main text.
Clinical CKD/dialysis context required before any general protein target.
Do not exchange food-group servings between plans or assume package serving equivalence.

releaseRequirements: clinical review of any personalized rule
privacy/provider gates before real health-data processing
